questions.q: Why does the summary say safety leads to progress?
a: People can only improve once basic needs and threats are handled
Safe teams avoid taking any kind of risk
Safety rules force people to work longer hours
Comfort makes people less ambitious over time
questions.why: Lesson 1 says our brains default to safety, so leaders who provide it free people to focus.

questions.q: What example does the summary use of a company with a strong circle of safety?
a: Google, with free food, open questions and time for experiments
A factory that tracks every minute of work
A bank that rewards only its top sellers
A startup that forbids employees from asking questions
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Google's perks as an environment where people can improve.

questions.q: What trait does the summary call the most important for a leader?
a: Empathy
Decisiveness
Charisma
Technical skill
questions.why: Lesson 2 says empathy lets you care about people and be worth following.

questions.q: What happened at the Peanut Corporation of America?
a: It shipped contaminated peanuts to protect cash flow
It recalled products before anyone became ill
It gave all of its profits to employees
It closed after a long labor dispute
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses it as an example of detached leaders harming people.

questions.q: What does the summary say technology does to us?
a: It turns us into performance addicts chasing quick dopamine hits
It makes us more patient and reflective
It reduces our need for social approval
It improves our long-term memory
questions.why: Lesson 3 says likes and small wins substitute for harder, lasting achievements.
